title: Console: experiment assignment middleware (sticky bucketing + holdouts)
author: Jin Woo Park
body:
Summary: Adds a small experimentation assignment layer for the Console to support the lifecycle growth sprint onboarding nudges (checklist + banners). This implements (1) sticky bucketing (stable assignment per user/project), (2) first-class holdout support, and (3) an explicit assignment payload that is attached to analytics events so we can analyze treatment effects cleanly.

Context / Why: For the onboarding nudges we need reliable randomization at the right unit (project for most nudges; user for a few global banners) and we need a guaranteed holdout to avoid “everyone eventually sees the nudge” creep. We also need assignments to be stable across page loads and device refreshes, but not depend on third-party experimentation vendors for the first iteration.

Design: The Console request pipeline now includes an ExperimentAssignmentMiddleware that runs early (before route rendering). Inputs: user_id (preferred), else anonymous_id from first-party cookie; project_id when available. We compute a deterministic bucket using HMAC-SHA256(seed, `${experimentKey}:${unitId}`) and map to [0,1). Each experiment declares: key, unit (user|project), traffic (0..1), holdout (0..1), variants (named with weights), and start/end gates. Holdout: if in holdout range, assignment is {variant: "holdout", in_holdout: true}. Otherwise, variant is selected by cumulative weights. Sticky: because it’s deterministic, the same unitId will always compute the same bucket (unless the seed changes).

Operational notes: The seed is read from CONSOLE_EXPERIMENT_SEED (required in prod/staging). In dev/test we default to a fixed seed and log a warning. This PR also adds a small admin/debug panel (hidden behind ?exp_debug=1 and internal role) that shows current assignments and unit ids to help QA verify bucketing.

Analytics: We attach experiment assignments to product events under `experiments: { [key]: { variant, in_holdout } }` (server-side) and expose a helper so client-side events can include the same payload without recomputing. This is intended to line up with the activation funnel instrumentation work in ENG-2841/PR #8932.

Guardrails / Privacy: No new identifiers are collected; we use existing console user_id/project_id and the existing anonymous cookie. We do not write variant names into cookies/localStorage (only rely on deterministic computation). We also avoid logging full unit ids in server logs (debug view only; redacted in standard logs).

How to test: 1) `pnpm console dev` and sign in. 2) Append `?exp_debug=1` to `/console` and confirm assignments appear. 3) Toggle between two test users and confirm sticky behavior. 4) Set `CONSOLE_EXPERIMENT_SEED=seedA`, confirm assignment; change to `seedB`, confirm assignment changes (expected). 5) Run `pnpm test console -- assignment`.

Rollout plan: Land behind a config gate; no experiments enabled by default. Growth sprint experiments will be added in a follow-up PR (nudges) using this assignment primitive. Holdout default for the sprint: 10% (configurable per experiment). Rollback: remove middleware registration; no schema changes.

Links: Linear ENG-2842. Related: PR #8932 (event schema), PR #8938 (checklist UI), PR #8950 (guardrail hooks).
commits: console/experiments: add experiment config schema + types
console/analytics: attach experiment payload to event context
tests: add unit tests for bucketing stability + holdout behavior
conversation: Jada Williams (review): Can we confirm the randomization unit for checklist vs banners? I want project-level for checklist steps so teammates don’t see conflicting states. Also +1 on not persisting variant in cookies.

Jin Woo Park (author): Yep — unit is per-experiment. Default helpers are `unit: "project"` when project_id exists, else it falls back to user_id/anon. Follow-up nudges PR will set checklist experiments to project. I’ll add a comment + test to prevent accidental user-level for checklist keys.

Paula Mendes (review): Please make sure the assignment context is attached server-side for ALL analytics events emitted from the console backend, not only UI events, otherwise analysis will be messy. Also: variant naming should be stable (no free-form copy strings).

Jin Woo Park (author): Updated `withExperimentContext` so both server-emitted and proxied client events get the same `experiments` payload. Variant values are constrained to the config enum; debug panel displays names but does not allow editing.

Logan Wright (review): One concern: seed rotation will re-bucket everyone. That’s fine but we should call it out in docs + require seed in prod. Also schema: can we cap payload size? Don’t want unbounded experiment keys sent on every event.

Jin Woo Park (author): Added env validation (required in prod/staging) and doc note about rotation. Also added `EXPERIMENT_ASSIGNMENT_MAX_KEYS` default=25; middleware only includes enabled experiments and truncates with a warning metric if exceeded.

Sean Gallagher (review): Perf: this middleware runs per request; any chance HMAC + iterating experiments adds noticeable overhead on dashboard load? Please add a micro-benchmark or at least a timing metric behind debug.

Jin Woo Park (author): Added a lightweight timing metric (`console.experiments.assignment_ms`) sampled at 1% and confirmed p95 < 0.4ms in staging. Also avoids crypto per experiment by reusing a keyed hash helper. Notes in docs.

Marissa Cole (review): Approving contingent on: (1) debug panel hidden for non-internal users, (2) no PII in logs by default, (3) holdout variant spelled exactly "holdout" so downstream queries are consistent.
Jin Woo Park (author): Done — debug panel requires internal role + query param, logs redact unit ids, and holdout variant constant is `HOLDOUT_VARIANT = "holdout"` with tests.
Merge: Squash and merge by Jin Woo Park. Commit message: "Console: experiment assignment middleware (sticky bucketing + holdouts) (#8941)"
release_notes: Internal: adds console experiment assignment primitive (sticky bucketing + holdouts) for lifecycle growth sprint; no user-visible changes until experiments are enabled.
